findings.title: Stored XSS via unescaped embed_url interpolated into raw_html post
findings.body:
TopicEmbed#import builds a trailing reference by interpolating the caller-controlled url directly into an HTML attribute and text node: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The url argument originates from arbitrary RSS items (PollFeed) or remote article fetches (import_remote), so an attacker controlling the feed/article can put characters like `'`, `>`, `"` into url to break out of the attribute or the link text. Because the contents are then stored as a post with `cook_method: raw_html` (which skips PrettyText/Markdown sanitization entirely, see app/models/post.rb#cook), the HTML is served verbatim to anyone rendering that post. Consequence: persistent XSS in Discourse via crafted RSS/ATOM items.

findings.title: XSS in embed layout: HTML-escaped referer inside a JS string literal
findings.body: The postMessage call interpolates `request.referer` into a single-quoted JS string with `<%= request.referer %>`, which only HTML-escapes output. Inside `<script>`, HTML entities such as `'` are unescaped by the JS parser back to `'` before execution, so a parent page can supply a referer like `https://x'); alert(1); //` and execute attacker JS in the embed iframe. The whole script must be emitted with JS-string-escaping (CGI.escape / json_escape or equivalent) rather than the default HTML escape, e.g. by using `j` and a JSON-encoded value or by replacing `'` with `\'`.

findings.title: Migration backfills cook_method=1 (raw_html) for every post, breaking cooking pipeline
findings.body: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` sets the integer 1 as the default for all existing rows and for every future insert that omits cook_method. But `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` in app/models/post.rb, where the Enum assigns sequential indices starting at 0, so `:regular == 0` and `:raw_html == 1`. The migration therefore marks every existing post as raw_html. After deployment, `before_save` (`self.cooked = cook(raw, topic_id: topic_id) unless new_record?`) calls `Post#cook`, which now short-circuits to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so the first edit on any previously-rendered post overwrites `cooked` with raw markdown and breaks rendering for that post and every post that quotes/redisplays it.

findings.title: Post.cook short-circuits to raw_html because the migration default points at the raw_html enum value
findings.body: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` is gated on the raw_html enum value, but the DB default set by the new migration (default: 1) and every PostCreator call that does not explicitly pass `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:regular]` will land on raw_html. Combined with the migration defaulting all rows to 1, every legacy post and every default-created post loses its cooked HTML. The intent appears to be that `raw_html` is opt-in (only the embed/RSS import path sets it), so the enum value used for the column default must be `:regular` (0) and any feed/import caller should pass the raw_html value explicitly. Right now, both kinds of writes converge on raw_html, corrupting posts.

findings.title: TopicRetriever invokes scheduled feed poll synchronously inside an embed job
findings.body: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` is called inline inside `perform_retrieve` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. PollFeed is a recurring scheduled job that fetches the full configured RSS/ATOM feed and imports every item; running it synchronously inside an embed fetch blocks the worker for the full poll duration, doubles the load on the feed endpoint (once from the scheduled worker, once from each embed call), and re-imports items outside the dedup logic embedded in TopicEmbed.import. It should enqueue the scheduled job via Sidekiq or at minimum only check `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...)` without triggering a full re-poll.

findings.title: NoMethodError when SiteSetting.embed_by_username is blank
findings.body: `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` calls `.downcase` on the setting value without first verifying it is non-nil. PollFeed guards against this with the `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` check, but `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` does not, so a missing setting raises NoMethodError, which propagates out of the retrieve_topic job. Guard with `return if SiteSetting.embed_by_username.blank?` like PollFeed does.

findings.title: NoMethodError or encoding crash on RSS items missing content
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` is a String that responds to scrub. SimpleRSS may leave `content` nil for entries without a `<content>` element, in which case the lookup raises NoMethodError on nil and aborts the entire poll (also no per-item rescue). On top of that, the surrounding code never validates the feed URL protocol, content type, or item count, and never catches network or parse errors, so a single malformed item or transient feed failure kills the whole job. Add nil guards (`i.content.to_s.scrub`) and per-item exception handling.

findings.title: Referer-based authorization is fragile and bypassable
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` only checks `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The Referer header is freely spoofable in many environments (browsers with privacy extensions, server-side fetchers, embedded webviews, curl), it can be wholly absent (in which case the empty string still passes URI parsing and compares mismatched, denying the request), and the comparison is a plain string match that ignores ports/scheme. An attacker able to set Referer (or to load the embed URL from a non-browser context) can pretend to come from any host. Authorization must not rely on a header that the configured embeddable host cannot enforce, and should additionally match scheme/port (e.g. compare `host_with_port` and `scheme`). At minimum, the current check must be paired with a signed/shared-secret or signed embed_url before the controller will fetch arbitrary content from the Discourse server.

findings.title: force: true silently drops and recreates the top_topics table
findings.body: Changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` makes the migration drop any pre-existing `top_topics` table before recreating it. The migration was previously already shipped to production; if any environment has a partially applied state, the next migration run will silently destroy data. Either drop the existing migration in favor of a new one that no-ops for upgrades, or document that this change must run on a clean DB only.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses indexOf substring match
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` checks whether `e.origin` appears anywhere inside `discourseUrl` rather than comparing the origin exactly. Even though discourseUrl is configured by the embedding site, a confused deployer can be tricked into rejecting legitimate messages or accepting unexpected ones if the configured URL embeds other origins as substrings. Use `discourseUrl.startsWith(e.origin + '/')` or compare origins directly.

findings.title: Unused require_dependency 'email/sender'
findings.body: The job requires `email/sender` but never references it (and TopicRetriever does not either). Remove the unused dependency to avoid loading unnecessary code paths and to prevent surprising coupling when email/Sender changes.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the perform_retrieve (SSRF and dedup) paths
findings.body: The spec only exercises the gated path through `retrieve` and asserts that `perform_retrieve` is or isn't called. There is no coverage of `perform_retrieve`, `fetch_http`, the `Jobs::PollFeed` invocation, or the duplicate-embed short-circuit. SSRF (fetching arbitrary URLs via `import_remote`) and the dedup queries are security-/data-integrity-sensitive and should have explicit specs covering the host check inside perform_retrieve, the user lookup, and the `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` early-return.
